entries.note: A hedged ('I think') view about a leading indicator. Neither 'things collapsing' nor 'one of the first signs' has a shared test.

entries.test: Whether NVIDIA's revenue keeps depending on a handful of hyperscalers buying GPUs at ever-higher prices and volumes each year, and whether it falters when that spending stops growing.
entries.note: Customer concentration can be checked now in NVIDIA's filings. But 'entire future is built on the idea' is a claim about the future and can only be tested if hyperscaler spending slows.
The antecedent 'if anything changes here' has no clear threshold, so it can't be said when it has been met. The $95bn commitments figure in the claim can be checked separately in the 10-K.

entries.test: Whether OpenAI fails as a going concern (bankruptcy, distressed sale or shutdown) after struggling to close its roughly $100bn round.
entries.note: 'I don't see how it's possible' is read as firm expectation, not probability language.

Applied Digital's and CoreWeave's filings on the North Dakota (Ellendale) campus, comparing lease revenue at full utilisation with debt service and operating costs.
entries.note: This is a claim about the project's economics, not a causal mechanism.

entries.test: Whether there are documented cases of a developer using Claude Code to replicate the core functionality of a mid-market SaaS product in weeks, well enough to replace a paid renewal.
entries.note: Calling it a 'lie' implies intent, which can't be tested. Only the capability claim can be graded.

entries.test: Whether legacy software stocks (e.g. SAP, software indices) fell in early 2026, with market coverage attributing the drop to fears that AI will disrupt software.
entries.note: Calling the fear a 'myth' is his judgment. The sell-off and its stated cause can be checked.

entries.test: Whether well-known published accounts of people impressed by Claude Code include non-trivial, novel software rather than only toy apps or template-like sites.
entries.note: The universal 'every example' is hyperbolic. One credible counterexample would falsify it.

entries.test: Whether a CRM that Claude Code generates from a simple prompt can be deployed, run securely and meet compliance requirements without substantial engineering work.
entries.note: The differentiation point is hedged ('I assume'), and 'if not more' engineers is a hedge.
'LLMs don't know anything' is a philosophical premise that readers would test in different ways.
The drafter's version drops 'rational': he says there is no *rational* basis, not that there is no other basis. Whether a sell-off is rational has no shared test.

entries.test: A survey of the authors of prominent articles praising Claude Code, showing what share are non-engineers or have commercial ties to AI.
entries.note: 'Captured' and 'burp up its training data' are rhetoric. Only the claim about who the authors are can be graded.
